```{python}
import json

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown

s = json.load(open("outputs/summary.json"))
profiles = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
rho = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant.csv").set_index("cluster")
k = s["k"]
names = profiles["name"].to_dict()
features = ["irca", "water_coverage", "sewer_coverage", "ipm", "rural_share", "altitude_m",
            "rainfall_mm", "mdm", "log_sgp_water_pc"]
labels = ["IRCA", "Piped water", "Sewer", "Poverty", "Rural share", "Altitude", "Rainfall",
          "MDM", "log SGP / person"]
```

# Introduction

Unsafe drinking water remains a public-health concern in rural Colombia. We ask which
kinds of municipal zone exist in terms of water risk, services and context, and how health
and education outcomes differ between them. Water risk is the utility-supplied
("prestadores") IRCA published by INS [@ins_irca], scored and banded under Resolución 2115
de 2007 [@res2115].

# Methods

## Data

The unit is a municipality's urban or rural zone in one year. Features come from INS
[@ins_irca], DNP TerriData [@terridata], DANE [@dane_divipola; @dane_pop; @dane_mgn],
CHIRPS rainfall [@funk2026; @funk2015; @chirps3data] and SRTM altitude [@srtm]; outcomes
from TerriData (infant mortality), ICFES [@icfes] and MEN [@men]. We keep
`{python} f"{s['kept']:,}"` municipality zone-years with an IRCA value, 2016–2023.

## Standardisation and clustering

Each feature $x_f$ is standardised within its year $t$,
$$
z_{if} = \frac{x_{if} - \bar{x}_{f,t}}{s_{f,t}},
$$ {#eq-z}
and k-means [@lloyd1982] chooses centres $m_c$ that minimise the within-cluster sum of
squares
$$
W = \sum_{c=1}^{k} \sum_{i \in C_c} \lVert z_i - m_c \rVert^2 .
$$ {#eq-kmeans}
We fit @eq-kmeans for $k = 2, \dots, 8$ with 20 starts and choose $k$ by the elbow of $W$,
checked with the mean silhouette [@rousseeuw1987]
$$
s(i) = \frac{b(i) - a(i)}{\max\{a(i), b(i)\}},
$$ {#eq-silhouette}
where $a(i)$ is the mean distance from $i$ to its own cluster and $b(i)$ to the nearest
other cluster. Stability across seeds is measured with the adjusted Rand index
[@hubert1985].

# Results

The analysis chose $k = `{python} k`$ (silhouette `{python} f"{s['silhouette_at_k']:.3f}"`;
ARI across seeds ≥ `{python} f"{s['ari_min']:.3f}"`). @fig-heatmap shows what sets the
kinds apart; @tbl-kinds lists them.

```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Cluster mean z-scores (@eq-z) by feature. IRCA is utility-supplied (prestadores)."
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap of four clusters by nine features from blue (below average) to red (above average)."
z = profiles[[f"z_{f}" for f in features]].to_numpy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 2.8))
im = ax.imshow(z, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1.5, vmax=1.5, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(features)), labels, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(range(k), [f"Cluster {c}" for c in profiles.index], fontsize=8)
for i in range(z.shape[0]):
    for j in range(z.shape[1]):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{z[i, j]:+.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="z")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-kinds
#| tbl-cap: "The kinds, with median utility-supplied (prestadores) IRCA and within-kind Spearman ρ between IRCA and infant mortality."
t = pd.DataFrame({"kind": profiles["name"], "zone-years": profiles["rows"],
                  "median IRCA": profiles["irca_median"],
                  "ρ": rho["spearman_rho"].map("{:+.2f}".format), "n": rho["n"]})
Markdown(t.to_markdown())
```

# Conclusions

The kinds differ far more in the features that formed them than in outcomes, and within
each kind infant mortality hardly varies with IRCA band. These comparisons are descriptive:
poverty, rurality, health-service access and reporting quality may confound them, and
infant mortality is municipal while IRCA is zonal. They do not establish causal effects of
water quality.
